docs.title: 🔐 Encrypted SQLite JSON & Two-Tier Caching Engine
docs.text:
A high-performance, thread-safe, AES-128 encrypted SQLite document store and Two-Tier (L1/L2) caching engine for Python applications, Discord bots, and microservices.

Serves as a transparent, high-speed drop-in replacement for standard flat .json file storage with sub-millisecond memory caching and zero-lock concurrency.

docs.title: 🌟 Highlights
docs.text:
• 🔒 AES-128 Fernet Encryption at Rest: All documents are encrypted before touching disk.
  • ⚡ Two-Tier (L1/L2) Caching:
    • Tier 1 (L1 RAM): Thread-safe LRU cache (< 0.01ms read latency).
    • Tier 2 (L2 Storage): SQLite in WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode.
  • 🔄 Write-Through Synchronization: Keeps RAM and encrypted SQLite in 100% sync.
  • 🛡️ Zero Thread Contention: Fully multi-threaded with thread-local connections.
  • 📦 Zero-Config Drop-in: Replace json.load() and json.dump() with load_json() and save_json().

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Generate an Encryption Key
docs.text:
python generate_key.py

Set the key in your .env or environment: 

ENCRYPTION_KEY=your_fernet_encryption_key_here=

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from src.secure_json import load_json, save_json

# 1. Save data (Write-Through to RAM + Encrypted SQLite)
save_json("user_101.json", {"username": "Alex", "level": 42, "xp": 189343})

# 2. Instant Load (<0.01ms from RAM)
data = load_json("user_101.json")
print(data["username"], data["level"])

docs.title: load_json(path, default=None)
docs.text:
Load and decrypt a JSON document using Two-Tier Caching (L1 RAM ➔ L2 SQLite fallback).

  • Arguments:
    • path (str | Path): File name or path (e.g. "settings.json").
    • default (Any, optional): Value returned if key is not found (default: {}).
  • Returns: Decrypted Python dictionary or list.

docs.title: save_json(path, data, indent=2)
docs.text:
Encrypt and persist data to L1 RAM, L2 SQLite, and atomic disk backup.

  • Arguments:
    • path (str | Path): File name or path.
    • data (Any): JSON-serializable Python object.
    • indent (int, optional): JSON indentation formatting (default: 2).

docs.title: cache.get(key, default=None)
docs.text: Retrieve a document from L1 RAM cache (or fall back to L2 SQLite).

docs.title: cache.set(key, data, ttl=None)
docs.text: Store an item with optional Time-To-Live expiration in seconds.

docs.title: cache.invalidate(key)
docs.text: Purge key from L1 RAM and delete from L2 SQLite.

docs.title: cache.get_stats()
docs.text:
Returns live cache metrics: 

{
    "l1_items_cached": 42,
    "l1_max_capacity": 1000,
    "hits": 1420,
    "misses": 31,
    "hit_ratio_str": "97.8%"
}

docs.title: db_maintenance()
docs.text: Executes SQLite WAL checkpoint truncation and index optimization: * PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE); * PRAGMA optimize;

docs.title: 🏛️ Architecture & Caching Design
docs.text: The system implements a formal Two-Tier (L1/L2) Hierarchical Caching Engine combined with AES-128 Fernet Encryption at Rest.

docs.title: 📊 Latency & Storage Hierarchy
docs.text: Tier Layer Media Typical Latency Description Tier 1 (L1) Application Cache System RAM < 0.01 ms Thread-safe LRU in-memory cache Tier 2 (L2) Persistent Store SSD / NVMe ~ 1.00 ms AES-128 Encrypted SQLite Database Fallback Safety Snapshot Local Disk ~ 2.50 ms Atomic encrypted .json file backup

docs.title: 🔄 Read Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor App as Application / Bot
    participant L1 as Tier 1: L1 RAM (LRU)
    participant L2 as Tier 2: L2 SQLite (WAL)
    participant Cipher as AES-128 Cipher

    App->>L1: load_json("user_101.json")
    alt L1 Cache Hit (<0.01ms)
        L1-->>App: Return deserialized dict immediately
    else L1 Cache Miss
        L1->>L2: SELECT value FROM kv_store WHERE key=?
        L2->>Cipher: Decrypt raw bytes
        Cipher-->>L2: Plaintext JSON string
        L2->>L1: Store into L1 RAM (warm up cache)
        L1-->>App: Return deserialized dict
    end

docs.title: 💾 Write Flow (Write-Through)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor App as Application / Bot
    participant L1 as Tier 1: L1 RAM (LRU)
    participant Cipher as AES-128 Cipher
    participant L2 as Tier 2: L2 SQLite (WAL)
    participant Disk as Encrypted Disk File

    App->>L1: save_json("user_101.json", data)
    L1->>L1: Update in-memory LRU cache
    L1->>Cipher: Encrypt JSON to ciphertext
    Cipher->>L2: INSERT INTO kv_store (key, value, ts) ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
    Cipher->>Disk: Atomic write to user_101.json.tmp -> replace
    Disk-->>App: Write complete & synchronized

docs.title: 🖥️ Command Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: The package includes a built-in encrypted-sqlite CLI command to manage and inspect your database.

docs.title: 1. Generate Encryption Key
docs.text: encrypted-sqlite keygen

docs.title: 2. View Database & Cache Stats
docs.text:
encrypted-sqlite stats
Sample Output: 
============================================================
 DATABASE & CACHE TELEMETRY
============================================================
 Database Path : data/app_database.db
 Database Size : 2.84 MB
 Stored Keys   : 147 documents

 Tier 1 (L1 RAM Cache):
 - Cached Items : 42 / 1000
 - Cache Hits   : 1420
 - Cache Misses : 31
 - Hit Ratio    : 97.8%
============================================================

docs.title: 3. Export Decrypted JSON Files
docs.text:
Export all encrypted database documents into a folder of plain-text .json files: 

encrypted-sqlite export --out ./backup_json/

docs.title: 4. Import JSON Files into Database
docs.text:
Scan a folder of .json files and import them into the encrypted database: 

encrypted-sqlite import ./my_data/

docs.title: 5. Inspect a Specific Document
docs.text: encrypted-sqlite get user_101.json

docs.title: 6. Run Database Maintenance
docs.text: encrypted-sqlite vacuum
